standards.summary:
The 100% claim is refuted on missing statements, one added item and grade placement. Statement wording holds up exactly.

Method: I fetched all 93 standard sets live from api.commonstandardsproject.com with a browser User-Agent. A statement is a standard that has no children (child links taken from parentId, or from ancestorIds when parentId is missing); anything with children is a heading. I matched each course outcome against those statements. Scripts and raw data are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-hassanahmed-ai-tutor/82ec5084-4ed0-4cc4-b280-430a6093d366/scratchpad/stdcheck/ (fetch.py, check.py, heads.py, raw/).

What holds:
- All 2,353 course outcomes match a source description exactly, ignoring only whitespace and HTML, with zero code mismatches.
- Each course uses every current standard set for its subject in the jurisdiction listing.

What fails:
1. **Missing statements (us-nc-arts, 4):** when two arts disciplines in the same grade share a statement with the same code and wording, only one copy is kept. Dropped: Theatre 1.RE.2.2; one of the Music/Theatre copies of 2.PR.2.1; one of the Theatre/Visual Arts copies of 5.CR.2.2 and of AD.CR.2.2. This matches mergeRows in lib/curriculum/build.ts, which keeps one row per code and text.
2. **One heading added as an outcome (us-nc-arts):** 'B.CN.2 Explore advancements in the field of dance.' is a heading in the Dance HS Beginning set (its two children point to it through ancestorIds; parentId is null in the source). It and its children are filed under 'High School Beginning' instead of CONNECT > B.CN.2. A similar case not counted: Nebraska grade 2 'Movement' is an empty topic heading shown as an outcome.
3. **Wrong grade labels (67 statements):** cspGrade in scripts/curriculum/structured.mts builds the label from the first and last entries of the source's educationLevels, which are not sorted.
   - MT Computer Science: K-4 shown as '1-K' (17 statements).
   - WY Physical Education: K-2 shown as '1-K' (16).
   - NC Arts: 9-12 Beginning General Music shown as '10-9' (20).
   - NE Social Studies: 9-12 Civics shown as '9-11', dropping grade 12 (14).
   - Also reversed but covering the right grades: NC '12-K' (22, split from the 'K-12' group) and VT 'K-PK' (18).
4. **Headings are not verbatim:** they match the source structure but are cut to about 70 characters. 'The student will' or 'Students will' and leading codes are removed, and some subtopics gain '(1 of 2)'.
5. **Faithful to the source but not teachable:** 41 placeholder outcomes such as 'Not applicable.', 'No standard at this level.', 'Incorporated into SES-MS-PS1-6.' and 'Not addressed at this level' (17 in WY Science, 24 in NE Social Studies). Nebraska also teaches about 82 high-school statements twice, because the ASN 9-12 set and the Common Curriculum high-school sets overlap.

Clean on statements, wording and grades: us-wy-science (282) and us-vt-physical-education (201); only the heading and label notes above apply to them.
